snp5.12:1.1: “Having heard of a hero who has no desire for sense pleasures,
snp5.12:1.3: I came to ask that desireless one who is beyond the flood,
snp5.12:1.4: please speak of the state of peace, conascent-eye,
snp5.12:1.5: as it really is, Fortunate One, please tell me this.
snp5.12:2.1: the Fortunate One moves about having vanquished sense desires,
snp5.12:2.2: as the splendid sun (vanquishes) the earth with its splendour.
snp5.12:2.3: To me of little wisdom, O One of Great Wisdom,
snp5.12:2.4: explain the Teaching so that I may know
snp5.12:2.5: the complete giving up of birth and old age here.”
snp5.12:3.3: having seen there is safety in renunciation;
snp5.12:3.4: let there be nothing found in you that has been taken up or put down.
snp5.12:4.1: You should erase that which is past,
snp5.12:4.2: and have nothing for the future,
snp5.12:4.3: if you take up nothing in the present
snp5.12:5.1: For one altogether without greed for mind and body, O brahmin,
snp5.12:5.4: whereby he can come under Death’s control.”
